mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs dampen economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a quarter indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate revenues and earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased consumer spending and corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or the joint effect of UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate earnings in related sectors.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals a reduction in inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate potential monetary easing and improved corporate profitability.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL declines and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% in a quarter signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters where GDPC1 increases by more than 1%, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
